# The invariants a pattern search can refuse.
#
# This file is the authority for which rules exist. The workflow at
# .github/workflows/greppable-invariants.yml supplies the machinery that decides
# each one and nothing else: a rule is added by adding a record here, so that
# adding a rule is a change somebody reads rather than an edit inside a script.
#
# Record format. A record ends at a line holding only three dashes. A line
# starting with # is a comment and a blank line is ignored. Every field is one
# line, and its value is everything after the first colon followed by a space,
# so a pattern that needs a literal colon before a space writes that space as
# the bracket expression [ ] instead.
#
# The fields, all four required:
#
#   id       a stable name. It is printed in every verdict and it is what the
#            two fixture files are named after, so renaming it without renaming
#            them fails the run rather than silently dropping the rule.
#   pattern  a POSIX extended regular expression, handed to git grep -E.
#   scope    one git pathspec saying where the rule applies. The fixture
#            directory is excluded from every scan by the workflow, because the
#            fixtures hold the violation on purpose.
#   reason   the failure this rule prevents, and where the rule stops.
#
# Every rule carries two fixtures, and the run refuses a rule that is missing
# either one:
#
#   .github/invariant-fixtures/<id>.refused.txt
#       Every line indented by four spaces is a violation and the pattern has to
#       match it. The run compares the set of line numbers the pattern matched
#       against the set of indented line numbers and requires them to be equal,
#       so a rule that lost one of its alternatives fails here instead of going
#       quietly green over a clean tree.
#
#   .github/invariant-fixtures/<id>.accepted.txt
#       The near miss. Legal text sitting one token away from the violation, and
#       the pattern has to match none of it. A rule that also refuses the legal
#       thing beside the violation is a rule whoever meets it turns off.
#
# What is not here yet, so a file that has grown is not read as a complete one.
# #91 names six rules. The copy-or-patch rule from #4 is here, in the two halves
# a content search decides. Three of the rest arrive with the thing they are
# about: the import rule with the units #37 separates, the pinned-version rule
# once there is a unit that depends on the version rather than a document
# quoting it, and the vocabulary rule with #63's list.
#
# Two parts of the copy-or-patch rule are absent and neither is waiting on code.
# #4 names a tracked file whose path ends in a patch or a diff extension, and
# that is decidable over paths rather than over content, which is not what this
# machinery does: every leg here hands a pattern to git grep and reads what is
# inside a file. A rule of that shape needs a leg that reads the file list, and
# adding one is a change to the workflow rather than a record here. The other
# part is #4's own residual, and it is the larger of the two: a file copied out
# of the suite and stripped of its banner matches nothing any pattern can write,
# and deciding that case needs a comparison against the upstream tree at the
# pinned tag rather than a search.
#
# A seventh rule reached #91 after its body was written, so the six above are not
# the whole of what this file owes. Entry 2 of #1 was decided on 2026-08-09: the
# server carries AGPL-3.0 and the extensions carry LGPL-2.1, which is the licence
# of the suite they load into, and the comment that decides it sends the boundary
# between the two here as a pattern rule so that moving a file does not move its
# licence with it in silence:
#
#     gh api repos/iderex/reissbrett/issues/1/comments --jq '.[] | select(.body | test("grepbare Invariante")) | "\(.created_at) \(.html_url)"'
#     2026-08-08T22:39:02Z https://github.com/iderex/reissbrett/issues/1#issuecomment-5228532779
#
# Neither half of that rule is available, and the two are absent for different
# reasons. A path-level form of the boundary waits on the layout in #15, because
# docs/decisions/0100-the-licence-split-and-the-suite.md states the boundary over
# artefacts rather than over paths, deliberately, so that it does not decide the
# layout in passing. The half that would refuse a source file carrying the wrong
# licence header, or none, is a shape this machinery cannot decide at all: every
# leg here hands a pattern to git grep, and a missing header is an absence rather
# than a match. That is established in 0100 rather than suspected here, and it
# puts the header half beside the two parts of the copy-or-patch rule above,
# which are absent for the same kind of reason rather than for want of code.

id: no-absolute-home-path
pattern: ([A-Za-z]:\\Users\\|/home/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/|/Users/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+/)
scope: .
reason: A path inside somebody's home directory exists on one machine. In a document it sends a reader somewhere they do not have, and in a pasted command it makes the output impossible to reproduce, which is the defect class this board counts. Write $HOME, a tilde, %USERPROFILE% or a path relative to the repository root. The drive letter is matched in either case, because a lowercase one is the mistake that gets past a reader.
---

id: no-display-server-in-workflows
pattern: ([Xx][Vv][Ff][Bb]|[Xx]org|DISPLAY=|WAYLAND_DISPLAY)
scope: .github/workflows/
reason: A step that installs, starts or points at a display server makes the headless requirement in #31 a preference. Where this rule stops is worth more than what it covers: it reads the workflow files, so it refuses a display server that is declared in one, and it does not reach a test process that starts its own. The image already carries a server on its PATH, which #31 measured, so the second half needs a check over what the test process did and it is #31's rather than this file's.
---

id: no-suite-source-header
pattern: (This file is part of the [F]reeCAD CAx development system|for detail see the LICEN[C]E text file)
scope: .
reason: A file lifted out of the suite's source tree keeps the banner that tree's own files carry, because the banner is the first thing a copy keeps and the last thing somebody thinks to remove. #4 decided that this repository carries no copy of that tree and no patch against it, with no exception list, and this is one half of the pattern share of that rule. Both alternatives are needed: the sentence naming the suite is absent from the machining module's Python files, which are the ones this project would be most tempted to lift from, and those carry the licence line instead. Where the rule stops is larger than what it covers, and it is #4's own residual: a copy stripped of its banner matches nothing, and deciding that case needs a comparison against the upstream tree at the pinned tag. The second alternative reads the spelling upstream uses for its licence file, so the spelling this repository uses for its own is accepted beside it.
---

id: no-suite-source-clone-in-workflows
pattern: (clone.*[F]reeCAD/FreeCAD|repository:[ ]*[F]reeCAD/FreeCAD|submodule.*[F]reeCAD/FreeCAD)
scope: .github/workflows/
reason: A build step that fetches the suite's source and builds from it carries the same thing a tracked copy would, and #4 refuses it in the same sentence. Fetching a release artefact and shipping it unchanged is not this, which is what #11's bundle does and what #108 builds, so the alternatives are written to pass a read of the upstream repository's metadata and a download of one of its releases. Where the rule stops: it is a pattern over the lines of a workflow file, so a target sitting on the line after a continuation is not seen, and it does not reach whatever #16 adds outside that directory. The scope is the workflow directory rather than the whole of .github, because SECURITY.md sends a defect in the suite to the suite's own advisory route and that link is the policy working.
---
